title: Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports: what do they show, who sees names and what do they cost?
summary: The page is held because it treats the audit operation for usage-report privacy changes as an open question, although Microsoft documents UpdateUsageReportsPrivacySetting. The report routes, permissions and both controls are supported; the audit-search checklist also names a control missing from the table.

claims.where: summary; What it is
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center usage dashboards show how people use Microsoft 365 services, including Copilot.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports provide insight into how people in your organization use Microsoft 365 for business services.

claims.where: What it is: definition
claims.claim: Microsoft says the reports show who uses a service most and who barely uses it and might not need a Microsoft 365 license.
claims.quote: you can see who uses a service to the fullest extent and who barely uses it and might not need a Microsoft 365 license.

claims.where: What it is: How they work, first bullet
claims.claim: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, Reports > Usage > View more on a service card opens that service's report tabs.
claims.quote: Select View more from the at-a-glance activity card for a service (such as email or OneDrive) to see the report details page. On that page, different reports for the service are provided in tabs.

claims.where: What it is: How they work, reporting periods
claims.claim: Usage reports generally cover the last 7, 30, 90 and 180 days.
claims.quote: Usage reports are generally available for the last 7, 30, 90, and 180 days.

claims.where: What it is: reporting delay; Risks and limits: Data lags
claims.claim: Reports typically become available within 24 to 72 hours, sometimes taking several days.
claims.quote: The reports typically become available within 24 to 72 hours, but might sometimes take several days to become available.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot usage reporting periods
claims.claim: The Copilot usage report offers 7, 28, 90 or 180 days.
claims.quote: You can view the Microsoft Copilot report over the last 7, 28, 90, or 180 days.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot Credits reporting periods
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report offers 7 or 30 days.
claims.quote: You can view the Copilot Credits report over the last 7 or 30 days.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot usage report route
claims.claim: The Copilot usage report is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Copilot > Usage.
claims.quote:
On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Copilot.
On the report page, select the Usage tab to view adoption and usage metrics.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot Credits report route
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Credits.
claims.quote:
In the navigation menu, select Reports.
Select Usage.
On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Credits.

claims.where: What it is: alternative reporting-options route
claims.claim: Microsoft's reporting-options article describes Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Usage instead.
claims.quote:
To view reports, go to Reports > Usage.
Select Microsoft Copilot > Readiness or Usage:

claims.where: What it is: enabled users; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Copilot usage report shows enabled users, defined as users with Microsoft Copilot licences.
claims.quote: Enabled Users shows the total number of unique users in your organization with Microsoft Copilot licenses over the selected timeframe.

claims.where: What it is: active users; Why it matters
claims.claim: The Copilot usage report shows active users and which apps they use.
claims.quote: In the Adoption section, Adoption by app shows enabled users and active users of Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: What it is: prompts submitted
claims.claim: The Copilot usage report shows prompts submitted.
claims.quote: Total prompts submitted shows the total number of prompts users sent to Microsoft Copilot Chat during the selected time frame.

claims.where: What it is: Credits billing-policy coverage; Why it matters
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report covers credits used for Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies.
claims.quote: This report gives you visibility into credits used for your Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies.

claims.where: What it is: Credits breakdowns
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report shows credits used per user.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.where: What it is: Credits breakdowns
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report shows credits used per agent.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.where: What it is: Credits breakdowns
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report shows credits used per billing policy.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.where: What it is: Credits breakdowns
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report shows credits used per agent-user pair.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.where: What it is: identifying detail; Why it matters; Risks and limits
claims.claim: By default, all usage reports hide usernames, display names, groups and sites.
claims.quote: By default, all reports hide user information such as usernames, display names, groups, and sites to help companies support local privacy laws.

claims.where: What it is: Other Copilot reporting sources
claims.claim: Microsoft lists four reporting sources: the Microsoft 365 admin center, Viva Insights Copilot Analytics, Microsoft Purview audit logs, and Power Platform and Copilot Studio analytics.
claims.quote:
Microsoft Copilot offers four main sources for usage reports.
Microsoft 365 admin center
Viva Insights Copilot Analytics
Microsoft Purview audit logs
Power Platform & Copilot Studio Analytics

claims.where: What it is: Copilot Dashboard link
claims.claim: Viva Feature Access Management governs the Copilot Dashboard through the Viva Insights web app control.
claims.quote: Turning this control off disables the entire app, which includes the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, Copilot Analytics reports, and advanced analysis and admin tools.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: The tenant name-concealment setting is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org Settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote:
Select Org Settings.
On the Services tab, select Reports.
In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/admin/reportSettings updates the tenant usage-report concealment setting.
claims.quote:
Update tenant-level settings for Microsoft 365 reports.
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/reportSettings

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Global administrators can change the organisation setting to show concealed identifying information.
claims.quote: Global administrators can update the settings to display concealed information if your organization's privacy practices allow it.

claims.where: controls[0].note
claims.claim: The PATCH request body sets displayConcealedNames, with true concealing names.
claims.quote: displayConcealedNames | Boolean | If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risks and limits
claims.claim: The organisation concealment setting also applies to Microsoft Graph usage reports.
claims.quote: This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI and to the usage reports in Microsoft Teams Admin center.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risks and limits
claims.claim: The organisation concealment setting also applies to Power BI usage reports.
claims.quote: This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI and to the usage reports in Microsoft Teams Admin center.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risks and limits
claims.claim: The organisation concealment setting also applies to Teams admin center usage reports.
claims.quote: This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI and to the usage reports in Microsoft Teams Admin center.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Names are hidden by default
claims.claim: The concealment setting anonymises identifying information in exports as well as reports.
claims.quote: The Global administrator can hide identifiable information (using MD5 hashes) such as display name, group name, email, and Microsoft Entra user ID in the report and its export.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: first paragraph
claims.claim: The usage reports overview lists viewing roles but names no separate viewing licence as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports viewing license charge prerequisites. Read the cited activity-reports overview in full, including Before you begin and View licensing information; no separate viewing licence is named.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: first paragraph
claims.claim: The usage reports overview names no separate viewing charge as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports viewing license charge prerequisites. Read the cited activity-reports overview in full; it lists roles and subscription-dependent report availability but no separate viewing charge.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: perpetual licences
claims.claim: Usage reports do not include perpetual license models.
claims.quote: Usage reports don't include perpetual license models.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Credits report coverage
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report makes metered agent usage by users without a Microsoft Copilot licence visible.
claims.quote: If you configure pay-as-you-go, and users without a Microsoft Copilot license use metered agents in Copilot Chat, the data appears in the report.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Copilot Studio meter
claims.claim: The Credits report covers consumption from interactions with agents that spin the Copilot Studio meter.
claims.quote: from interactions by users in your organization who don't have a Microsoft Copilot license and are interacting with agents in Copilot Chat that spin the Copilot Studio meter during the selected time period.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Names are hidden by default
claims.claim: The same hidden-data setting controls the Billing Policy ID and user names in the Copilot Credits report.
claims.quote:
By default, the Copilot credits report anonymizes the Billing Policy ID, just like the username and display name.
Changes to this hidden data setting affect the username, display name, and Billing Policy ID.

claims.where: Risks and limits: The setting is a logged event; What to check
claims.claim: Showing identifiable user information is logged in the Microsoft Purview audit log.
claims.quote: Showing identifiable user information is a logged event in the Microsoft Purview portal audit log.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Role choice decides what a reader sees
claims.claim: Usage Summary Reports Reader has no user details in the admin center reports.
claims.quote: Usage Summary Reports Reader (with no user details).

claims.where: Risks and limits: Role choice decides what a reader sees
claims.claim: User Experience Success Manager has no user details in the admin center reports.
claims.quote: User Experience Success Manager (with no user details)

claims.where: Risks and limits: Graph role restrictions
claims.claim: Global Reader gets tenant-level data only through the Graph reports API.
claims.quote: The Global Reader and Usage Summary Reports Reader roles will only have access to tenant-level data, without visibility into detailed metrics.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Graph role restrictions
claims.claim: Usage Summary Reports Reader gets tenant-level data only through the Graph reports API.
claims.quote: The Global Reader and Usage Summary Reports Reader roles will only have access to tenant-level data, without visibility into detailed metrics.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Data lags
claims.claim: Copilot activity reporting typically takes about 48 hours.
claims.quote: For Copilot activity on a given day, the report typically becomes available within 48 hours of the end of that day (in UTC).

claims.where: Risks and limits: Data lags
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report does not automatically update for recent usage and must be refreshed manually.
claims.quote: The report shows data up to today, but it doesn't automatically update if there's recent usage. To view the latest data, manually refresh the report.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot Credits report history; What to check
claims.claim: During preview, the Copilot Credits report shows a maximum of 30 days of history.
claims.quote: During preview, the report displays a maximum of 30 days of Copilot Credits history.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot Credits report history; Open questions
claims.claim: Usage information from before 3 May 2025 is unavailable in the Copilot Credits report.
claims.quote: usage information from before May 3, 2025, isn't available in the report.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Alerts
claims.claim: The Credits report shows an Alerts card when a user consumes more than 3,000 credits in the past 30 days.
claims.quote: The Alerts card is visible in the report when one or more users consume more than 3,000 credits in the past 30 days.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Alerts
claims.claim: A similar Credits report alert appears when users consume 2,000 to 3,000 credits.
claims.quote: If users consume 2,000 to 3,000 credits, a similar alert appears.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Alerts are report cards, not limits
claims.claim: The Credits report's alert cards are not consumption caps.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Copilot Credits report Alerts card consumption limits stop cap enforcement. Read the Credits report and Cost Management overview; cards display alerts and details, while separate spending policies set caps. No report-card enforcement is documented.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Not every cloud has every report
claims.claim: The overview lists the Copilot Credits report as available in the public cloud only.
claims.quote:
Report | Public | GCC | GCC-High | DoD | Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet
Microsoft Copilot credits | Yes | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A

claims.where: Risks and limits: Not every cloud has every report
claims.claim: Other reports are not yet released in some clouds.
claims.quote:
Microsoft browser usage | Yes | N/A^1^ | N/A^1^ | N/A^1^ | N/A^1^
N/A^1^: The report will be released in the future.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No per-user lookup
claims.claim: The admin center reports cannot generate a cross-service usage list by entering a user account; service reports can instead be sorted or exported.
claims.quote: You can't generate a report where you enter a user's account and then get a list of which services they're using and how much.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted users disappear
claims.claim: Microsoft deletes a deleted user's usage data within 30 days.
claims.quote: When you delete a user account, Microsoft deletes that user's usage data within 30 days.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted users disappear
claims.claim: Usage chart totals still count deleted users for periods when they were active.
claims.quote: The usage chart totals still include deleted users for the periods they were active, but they don't appear in the User Details table.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot usage by Graph excludes unlicensed users
claims.claim: The Copilot usage API returns usage data only for users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: This API only returns usage data for users who have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: controls[1].ui
claims.claim: Reporting roles can be assigned at Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity > Users > All users > user > Assigned roles > Add assignment > role.
claims.quote:
Expand the Identity menu > Users > select All users.
Select the user.
Choose Assigned roles, and then Add assignment.
Select the appropriate role, and click Add.

claims.where: controls[1].api
claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments creates the Microsoft Entra role assignment that grants a user a reporting role.

Create a role assignment for the directory provider:

POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments

claims.where: controls[1].note
claims.claim: Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged role the Graph role-assignment reference names.
claims.quote: For delegated access using work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role that grants the permissions required for this operation. Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.

claims.where: controls[1].note
claims.claim: The role-assignment body sets roleDefinitionId to identify the reporting role.
claims.quote:
roleDefinitionId can be either the service-wide template Id or the directory-specific roleDefinitionId.
"roleDefinitionId": "c2cf284d-6c41-4e6b-afac-4b80928c9034"

claims.where: controls[1].note
claims.claim: The role-assignment body sets principalId to identify the user receiving the assignment.
claims.quote: principalId | String | Required. Identifier of the principal to which the assignment is granted.

claims.where: controls[1].note
claims.claim: The role-assignment body sets directoryScopeId to / for tenant-wide scope.
claims.quote: For the directory (Microsoft Entra ID) provider, this property supports the following formats: - / for tenant-wide scope

claims.where: Governance controls: API reader permission

claims.quote: Select Reports, and then choose to Display concealed user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.where: Open questions: audit operation name
claims.claim: The audit operation name for showing identifiable user information remains an open documentation question.
claims.quote:
Report activities
The following table lists the activities for usage reports recorded in the Microsoft 365 audit log.
Updated usage report privacy settings | UpdateUsageReportsPrivacySetting | Admin updated privacy settings for usage reports.
claims.fix: Remove the first Open questions bullet. Replace the existing logged-event sentence in Risks and limits with: 'Microsoft Purview records changes to usage-report privacy settings as UpdateUsageReportsPrivacySetting (Updated usage report privacy settings).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-activities#report-activities.

claims.where: Open questions: the overview does not name the event
claims.claim: The usage reports overview says the change is logged but does not itself name the audit operation.
claims.quote: Searched: usage reports showing identifiable user information audit operation name ReportSettingsUpdated conceal names. Read the activity-reports overview in full: it says the event is logged but contains no operation name; the separate Purview activity reference supplies it.

claims.where: Open questions: Credits history after preview
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the Credits report's preview history limits persist after preview.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Credits report history 30 days May 3 2025 after preview. Read the cited Credits report and returned report-history excerpts; they state the preview limit and historical gap, without specifying a post-preview history policy.

claims.where: What to check: Search the Microsoft Purview audit log
claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to search the audit log, but the controls table contains no audit-search row.
claims.quote: What to check: 'Search the Microsoft Purview audit log for the logged event when identifiable names were last shown.' The table contains only name concealment and reporting-role assignment.
claims.fix: The audit-search checklist step has no controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet; the existing linked auditing concept and logged-event discussion can remain. Do not add a control row as part of this correction.

claims.quote: Create, read, update, and delete spending policies that cap Copilot Credits consumption for an audience.
